Package org.smtlib.solvers

Class Solver_cvc5

java.lang.Object
org.smtlib.AbstractSolver
org.smtlib.solvers.Solver_cvc5
All Implemented Interfaces:
ISolver
public class Solver_cvc5 extends AbstractSolver implements ISolver
This class is an adapter for cvc5, on the assumption that it is (or should be) a fully SMT-LIB compliant solver: it is a concrete, silent inheritor of AbstractSolver — only the startup command line (cvc5 needs --incremental to accept push/pop at all, and --quiet to suppress informational stderr chatter that would otherwise fool SolverProcess's stdout/stderr-preference heuristic) and start() (process lifecycle) are overridden. Empirically (against cvc5 1.3.2), none of the CVC4-era workarounds a previous version of this class used to need still apply: cvc5 handles Bool-sorted quantifiers natively (no translate() workaround needed), get-value/ get-option return clean standard-shaped responses (no Response.Seq workaround needed), and get-info/get-option round-trip through AbstractSolver's generic parseResponse without issue -- with one exception, get_option(org.smtlib.IExpr.IKeyword), described below.

One confirmed, patchable compliance gap: cvc5 answers (get-option :regular-output-channel)/(get-option :diagnostic-output-channel) with a bare, unquoted symbol (stdout/stderr) rather than the SMT-LIB string literal ("stdout"/"stderr") these two options are specified to hold -- confirmed against a real cvc5 1.3.2 process. get_option(org.smtlib.IExpr.IKeyword) wraps a bare-symbol answer for either option into a proper string literal with the same text.

One confirmed, non-workaroundable compliance gap: cvc5 self-reports (get-info :error-behavior) as immediate-exit (not continued-execution) and its process actually exits after a top-level parse error. Neither (set-option :error-behavior continued-execution) (rejected as unsupported) nor (set-info :error-behavior continued-execution) (silently accepted but with no actual effect — get-info still reports immediate-exit and the process still dies) can change this, so there's no way to ask for the other mode. selfReportsImmediateExit() tells AbstractSolver.sendCommand(ICommand, boolean) about this, so once cvc5 reports one real error, jSMTLIB pauses briefly before sending anything further, giving the process time to actually finish exiting (if it is going to) before the next command's liveness check runs.

  • Method Details

    • selfReportsImmediateExit

      protected boolean selfReportsImmediateExit()
      Description copied from class: AbstractSolver
      Overridden by a subclass whose target solver's :error-behavior is immediate-exit (e.g. cvc5, yices2) rather than the SMT-LIB default of continued-execution -- such a solver's process may start exiting asynchronously right after it reports an error, and SolverProcess.send(boolean, String...)'s own process.isAlive() check can still read true for a brief window afterward (OS process-death bookkeeping lags the actual exit) -- see AbstractSolver.sendCommand(ICommand, boolean), which uses this to give a solver that just reported an error a moment to actually finish dying before the next command's liveness check runs, closing that race deterministically rather than guessing from the error's content whether the process will actually exit.
      Overrides:
      selfReportsImmediateExit in class AbstractSolver

    • errorStopsSolver

      protected boolean errorStopsSolver(IResponse error)
      cvc5 carries on after most errors (e.g. sort errors), but after a parse error it no longer processes input, and when run interactively it does not always exit either -- so it is stopped (see AbstractSolver.checkImmediateExit).
      Overrides:
      errorStopsSolver in class AbstractSolver

    • set_option_impl

      protected IResponse set_option_impl(IExpr.IKeyword key, IAttributeValue value)
      Description copied from class: AbstractSolver
      Override in subclasses to handle solver-specific options. Channel options are handled by set_option and never reach here. This default handles :print-success client-side (see AbstractSolver.checkPrintSuccess(org.smtlib.SMT.Configuration, org.smtlib.IExpr.IKeyword, org.smtlib.IAttributeValue)): the solver process is always left with :print-success true at the wire level (see start()/sendCommand()) -- without that, we'd get no acknowledgment at all for other commands once a script turns it off -- so it is answered entirely client-side, matching the local smtConfig.nosuccess flag, and is never itself forwarded to the solver process. A subclass that overrides set_option_impl for other reasons (e.g. to also track option values locally) needs its own checkPrintSuccess call, same as it always has -- this default is only reached by a subclass that doesn't override set_option_impl at all.
      Overrides:
      set_option_impl in class AbstractSolver
